problem_statement:
Add an ACP (Agent Client Protocol) stdio server so editors can drive Wells

Wells can already run a task headlessly (`wells -p --output-format json`). Editors that speak ACP (Zed, JetBrains, other clients) need a long-lived agent process they talk to over stdio using JSON-RPC 2.0. Add one.

Deliverable: a new module `src/wells/acp_server.py`, standard library only (json, sys, threading, contextlib, uuid). It must export `read_message`, `write_message`, `run_task`, `AcpServer`, `serve` and `main`. Also add a `wells-acp = "wells.acp_server:main"` entry under `[project.scripts]` in pyproject.toml.

Framing (LSP-style)
- `write_message(stream, message)` serialises `message` to UTF-8 JSON and writes `Content-Length: <byte count>\r\n\r\n` followed by the body.
- `read_message(stream)` reads one such message from a binary stream and returns the decoded dict. Return `None` at end of stream. Raise `ValueError` for a malformed frame: no `Content-Length` header, an oversized header, or a truncated body. The length counts bytes, not characters, so multi-byte UTF-8 must round-trip exactly.

Server
- `AcpServer(send=None, task_runner=run_task)`. `send` is called with every outgoing message, responses and notifications alike, including from the worker thread that runs prompts, so writes must be serialised. `task_runner(goal, cwd)` returns the result dict of one task.
- `handle_message(message)` processes one decoded message. A message that is not a JSON-RPC 2.0 object is answered with error code -32600 and id null. A notification (no `id`) never gets a response. A request for an unknown method is answered with -32601 and the method name in the error message. A handler that raises is answered with -32603 and never crashes the loop.

Methods
- `initialize` responds `{"protocolVersion": 1, "agentCapabilities": {"loadSession": false}, "authMethods": []}`.
- `session/new` takes `cwd` and responds `{"sessionId": <new uuid4 string>, "mode": {"kind": "primary", "name": "default"}, "mcpServers": []}`. The server records `sessions[sessionId] = cwd` (a public attribute named `sessions`).
- `session/prompt` takes `sessionId` and `prompt`, an ACP prompt object whose `content` is a list of blocks; join the text of its `text` blocks with newlines to get the goal. An unknown session is answered with -32600. Otherwise the work happens on a daemon worker thread and `handle_message` returns at once, so the read loop stays free to process `session/cancel` while the task runs.
- `session/cancel` takes `sessionId` and responds `{}`. It marks a running turn on that session as cancelled and calls `cancel()` on the control bus (`wells.control.CONTROL`). With nothing running it does nothing.
- `fs/read_text_file` is not supported: answer -32601.

Streaming a turn
Progress is reported as notifications of the form `{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "session/update", "params": {"sessionId": <id>, "update": {...}}}`. Every update carries a fresh integer `updateId` taken from a counter. A turn emits, in order: `{"sessionUpdate": "turn", "state": "start"}`; then, if the task produced message text, `{"sessionUpdate": "agent_message", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": ...}]}`; then `{"sessionUpdate": "turn", "state": "complete", "stopReason": ...}`. Only then is the `session/prompt` request itself answered, with `{"stopReason": ...}`. The stop reason is "cancelled" when the turn was cancelled and "end_turn" otherwise. If the task runner raises, the turn still completes (so the editor UI does not hang) and the request is answered with -32603 and the exception text.

Task runner
- `run_task(goal, cwd=None) -> dict` runs one headless task. When `cwd` is given, set `wells.config.WORKSPACE_ROOT` to it for the duration and restore the previous value afterwards. Call `wells.main._run_goal(goal, output_format="json")` with stdout redirected into a buffer; that function signals completion by raising `SystemExit`, which must be caught so the server keeps running. Return the JSON object it printed: scan the captured lines from the end and parse the first line that starts with `{`. If nothing was printed return `{"status": "error", "error": "no output from task runner"}`; if no line parses return `{"status": "error", "error": "unparseable output: <first 400 chars>"}`.
- The message text for a turn is built from the result dict: the non-empty string values of `summary`, `review_result` and `git_summary`, joined with a blank line; when `status` is "error" and there is an `error`, append "error: <error>".

Stdio loop
- `serve(stdin=None, stdout=None)` reads framed messages until end of input and passes each to an `AcpServer` whose `send` writes framed messages to the output stream (defaults: `sys.stdin.buffer` and `sys.stdout.buffer`). A frame that fails to parse is answered with -32700 and the loop continues. A failed write (the client has gone away) is ignored; the loop ends on the next read.
- `wait_for_prompts(timeout=10.0)` blocks until no prompt worker is in flight.
- `main()` calls `serve()`.
